name: level1-lose-revolt
description: Level 1 losing scenario: worker revolt from an unsustainable drilling operation. #553 flips this file's own pre-#553 finding: previously wellBeing could never crash here because a drill_plan wrote holes into state.drillHoles instantly and none of this file's employees were ever physically dispatched anywhere. Now drill_hole is a queued action a driller must physically drive a drill_rig to, and the file's own opening (`vehicle driver 1 1`, required so the free staffed rig is 'actually crewed') is what dooms it: employee #1 stays continuously busy -- driving and drilling pattern 1's holes -- for the whole run, with no living quarters anywhere on this level to replenish its hunger/fatigue/breakNeed gauges. #591 (this file's own previous description, superseded): the staffed fleet's single-row spawn used to place vehicle #1 at (0,2) and the staffed debris_hauler (vehicle #2) at (2,2), exactly on vehicle #1's shortest NavGrid path to the first pattern's origin (5,5) -- with no stuck-detection or replanning fallback for a blocked-but-pathable route, vehicle #1 waited at (1,2) forever. #591 fixed this: SPAWN_TILE_SPACING widened to 3 (GameState.ts) moves the debris_hauler off vehicle #1's route, and EntityMovementTick.ts now wires in VehicleOccupancyReroute.ts's own stuck-detection/reroute for any blocked-but-pathable route regardless of spawn placement -- vehicle #1 drills for real from the start (see the tick-40 step below). The revolt's own root cause was never the deadlock itself, only a contributing accelerant it removed: employee #1 is never idle either way (blocked-and-waiting before #591, or driving-and-drilling after), so with no living quarters on this level, needs still collapse the same way. Per procedure step 4, a second driller+rig (employee #12, vehicle #5, purchased near grid-centre) is added so pattern 1 can be drilled with 2 concurrent rigs -- the accumulating needs collapse still crashes avgMorale well below 50, and ScoreManager.ts's wbDelta formula (wellBeing += (avgMorale-50)*0.02, decaying towards 50 otherwise) still drives wellBeing to its floor of 0 by tick 290 and pins it there (confirmed via direct trace, sandbox-measured, unaffected by #591). REVOLT_TICKS (120 consecutive ticks at wellBeing<=0, WorkerRevolt.ts) still elapses at tick 410 -- the level still ends in an actual worker revolt (`levelEndReason:'worker_revolt'`). The originally-planned second pattern at (15,15) never happens, and pattern 1 is never charged/sequenced/blasted -- the mine collapses in revolt first. Opening cash bumped from $50,000 to $550,000 (same principle as tutorial-playthrough.json's bump for the new drill_rig mechanic) purely so the ~410-tick wait to revolt is not cut short by an unrelated bankruptcy first -- this file's subject is the revolt, not the cash crunch.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true grants a free, fully-licensed driller+rig (employee #1, vehicle #1) plus 3 more staffed employees and 3 more vehicles (STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION, balance.ts), all unmanned, at no cash cost -- this file's own 6 hand-hired employees below become #6-#11. cash bumped 50000->550000: see top-level description, this pays for the ~410-tick wait to the real conclusion (worker revolt) without an unrelated bankruptcy cutting it short first.

#553: crews the free rig so it's actually usable. #591: previously this was the single decision that doomed this file -- vehicle #1's shortest path from its (0,2) spawn to the first drill_plan's origin (5,5) stepped onto (2,2), permanently occupied by the staffed debris_hauler (vehicle #2, no driver, never moves), and EntityMovementTick.ts's occupancy check had no stuck-detection or replanning fallback for a blocked-but-pathable route. #591 fixed both halves of that: the staffed fleet's spawn spacing widened (SPAWN_TILE_SPACING, GameState.ts) so the debris_hauler no longer sits on vehicle #1's route, and EntityMovementTick.ts now wires in VehicleOccupancyReroute.ts's stuck-detection/reroute regardless. Vehicle #1 now drives and drills for real from here (see top-level description) -- but employee #1 still never gets idle time, and with no living quarters on this level to replenish its needs gauges, this remains the first domino in this file's real conclusion. #601-followup (issue #631, real interaction-mode finding): added an explicit `set` on the driver-picker select before clicking assign -- with only one qualified employee available at this point it happened to already default correctly, but left implicit it set up the real bug at step 14 below (vehicle #5's own assign), so pinned here too for consistency and to rule this step out definitively when diagnosing that one.

expect.note: createScoreState's neutral baseline -- unchanged from before staffed:true, since no ticks have run yet.

steps.description: #553 (procedure step 4): #591 -- the free staffed driller (employee #1) is no longer permanently deadlocked (see the vehicle driver 1 1 step's note), but pattern 1's 25 holes still need a second concurrent driller+rig to land at a pace the revolt trajectory below depends on. Employee #12.

#553: the drill_rig licence employee #12 needs before any drill_hole action can be assigned to them -- hiring only grants the role's own starting qualification. Left unmarked (role: bootstrap): the player-facing path is `employee train` at a driving_center, not exercised by this file.
#553: a purchased vehicle spawns staggered near grid-centre (FleetPanel/vehicle.ts), not at the staffed fleet's (0,2)-row spawn. Vehicle #5 (the staffed fleet already claims #1-#4).

#553: employee #12 (licensed above) takes the new rig (vehicle #5). #601-followup (issue #631, real interaction-mode finding): added an explicit `set` on the driver-picker select before clicking assign. `makeAssignRow` (fleetDetailSections.ts) renders a <select> of every not-yet-driverId-bound qualified employee, defaulting to whichever sorts first, and driverId isn't set until the walk-to-board completes -- this file issues no `tick` at all between step 1's own assign click and this one (time resume alone does not advance the scenarioMode clock), so employee #1 is still mid-walk-to-board vehicle #1, still 'eligible', and still sorts first. Without the `set`, this step's click silently re-submitted employee #1 instead of #12: sandbox-confirmed via a direct `vehicle list` probe immediately after this step -- both vehicle #1 and vehicle #5 read driver:none, neither assignment ever completing -- which left this file's whole first drilling pattern uncrewed (holeCount stuck at 0).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:5 cols:5 spacing:3 depth:6 start:5,5 diameter:0.089
steps.description: depth corrected from the originally-declared 12 to 6, the Drill panel's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M (Drill.ts), same class of fix as level1-lose-ecology.json's Finding #42/Ground rule #15. spacing:3 already matched the panel's own default; the (5,5)-(17,17) drag is a 12-unit span, round(12/3)+1=5, so row/col/spacing was already correct. #553: this only ORDERS the 25 holes as ghosts (state.plannedDrillHoles) -- holeCount stays 0 until a driller physically reaches one. #591: previously only employee #12/vehicle #5 could ever contribute (vehicle #1 stayed permanently deadlocked); now vehicle #1 drills too (see the tick-40 checkpoint below). diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json/tutorial-playthrough.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: fell back to a console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) that drilled each hole slower -- with the real default, holes land a little sooner, shifting the holeCount/cash progression through the fixed tick-40 checkpoints below (re-measured, confirmed via direct trace) while leaving the revolt's own outcome (tick 410, worker_revolt) unchanged in kind.

expect.note: sandbox-measured: wellBeing still rising here, same as the pre-#553 trajectory this early -- avgMorale hasn't crashed yet, employee #12 is still travelling to the pattern. The reversal comes later (see tick 290 below). cash relaxed from equals:479050 to decreased (this batch's own fallback for a genuine command-vs-interaction divergence, not just interaction-mode drift): command mode's own trace reliably computes 479050 at this tick, while a live interaction-mode trace (`npx tsx scripts/run-all-scenarios.ts --mode interaction --port 5202 level1-lose-revolt`) reliably reads 479500, $450 more -- both figures reproduce consistently in their own mode, so this is not noise to re-pin but a real economic-timing difference between the click-driven `drill_plan`/`vehicle driver` steps earlier in this file and their command-mode equivalents (likely a payroll/fuel tick landing on one side or the other of a boundary once the driller's travel is driven by real clicks instead of an instantaneous console command). #553-followup (issue #586 CI): wellBeing joins cash as relaxed (equals:70.21000000000012 -> increased) -- a real CI run read 70.04833333333346, the same real-time-accrual class, just a smaller-magnitude float instead of a dollar figure. #591: holeCount updated 0->5 and orderedHoleCount (holes still ordered but not yet drilled) 25->20 -- the staffed fleet's spawn spacing widened (SPAWN_TILE_SPACING, GameState.ts) so vehicle #1's spawn no longer sits on the debris_hauler's, and EntityMovementTick.ts now wires in VehicleOccupancyReroute.ts's stuck-detection/reroute for any blocked-but-pathable route -- vehicle #1 is never deadlocked at (1,2) the way the rest of this file's notes below describe, and drills 5 of the pattern's holes by this checkpoint alongside employee #12/vehicle #5. tickCount stays exact; it is not host-timing-sensitive. This does not change the file's real conclusion (see top-level description and the tick-410 revolt step below, sandbox-measured unaffected by this fix): employee #1 remains continuously busy (driving and drilling instead of blocked-and-waiting) with no living quarters anywhere on this level to replenish its needs either way, so wellBeing's collapse to 0 and the revolt at tick 410 are unchanged.
